name: Verisk Analytics, Inc. (ADJACENT - insurance data & analytics)

corporate_actions.event: Terminated agreement to acquire AccuLynx after extended FTC review; redeemed $1.5bn 2030/2036 notes issued for the deal on 6-Jan-2026

geography.fx_notes: ~83% US (PitchBook/Morningstar profile); remainder mainly UK/Europe (cat models, specialty).

kpis.name: FY2026 guidance
kpis.value: Revenue $3,190-3,240m; adj EBITDA $1,790-1,830m (56.0-56.5% margin); adj EPS $7.45-7.75 - reaffirmed Q3

acquisitions.notes: AccuLynx (~$2.35bn, announced 2025 - amount not re-verified) terminated; no large deal completed

management.senior_turnover_5y: Portfolio simplification 2021-23 (energy/Wood Mackenzie, financial services sold) under new leadership
management.guidance_record: FY26 guidance reaffirmed (toward midpoint); Q1-26 described as trough

guidance.value: revenue $3.19-3.24bn, adj EBITDA margin 56.0-56.5%, toward midpoint

evidence: Subscription revenue growing 8.2% OCC and the large majority of revenue (S2)
Embedded statutory/ISO forms and loss costs used by P&C insurers (S1)
A.rationale: >80% recurring subscription with very high retention (INFERENCE from model; retention % not extracted).

evidence: ISO statistical-agent data, policy forms and Xactimate claims estimating are industry standards (S1)
B.rationale: Unique contributory data and regulatory embedding create strong moat.

evidence: AccuLynx deal abandoned after FTC delay (S3)
$100m ASR Q3-26; AccuLynx terminated; buybacks at high multiples (S2)
Transactional revenue +3.2% only; claims (Xactimate) exposed to AI estimating (S2)
I1.rationale: Data moat strong, but analytics/claims software layers face AI-native competition - moderate, scored seriously given market concern (INFERENCE).

evidence: FCF down 40% in Q3-26 needs explanation (S2)

ai.notes: High AI-substitution relevance: genAI could lower barriers in underwriting analytics and claims estimating; ISO statutory data moat mitigates.

sector_specific.organic_ex_rate_note: Not a broker: subscription pricing loosely linked to insurer premium volumes; no direct rate pass-through.

gates.notes: G1: ~2.75x. G4: Q3-26 FCF -40% - lead agent to check 3y FCF/NI (historically ~100%).

bull_points: Irreplaceable ISO statutory data and Xactimate standard; 56% margins.
bear_points: AI could erode claims estimating/analytics differentiation; transactional growth only 3%.
Mature growth (6-8%) and US concentration; FCF weakness in Q3-26.
Failed AccuLynx deal leaves growth M&A uncertain.
thesis_breakers: OCC growth < 5% for a full year.
